rubric.evidence: WebIDL verified against W3C WebTransport CR/ED and Blink web_transport.idl; 255-byte label/context limits, 1-4096 byte outputLength bounds, connecting-state queueing (PendingExportKeyingMaterialRequest), fixed label 'EXPORTER-WebTransport', and SerializeWebTransportExporterContext wire framing verified directly in Blink web_transport.cc, net/quic/dedicated_web_transport_http3_client.cc, and WPT export-keying-material.https.any.js (fetched 2026-11-24).

Feature 4860330806214656 appears under 'Enabled by default' in /api/v0/features?milestone=159 with listing name 'WebTransport keying material export'; H1 matches listing name; declared ChromeStatus row links https://chromestatus.com/feature/4860330806214656.

Honest MDN stub (Case A): MDN WebTransport/exportKeyingMaterial returns HTTP 200 and documents the exact 3-arg Chrome 159 signature, 255/4096 bounds, RangeError/InvalidStateError rejections, TLS exporter theory, MitM detection, HMAC-SHA256 example, Specifications, and Browser compatibility (already listing Chrome 159). Adds Chromium's exact EXPORTER-WebTransport label + CONNECT stream ID context framing, connecting-state queuing, length === 3 detection, and BCD outputLength_parameter lag disclosure.

Explains exact HTTP/3 CONNECT stream ID domain separation for pooled sessions, why a server/client context mismatch fails silently with different bytes, and how to distinguish the 3-arg signature from Firefox 155-159's 2-arg form.

Concise 3-arg feature-detection and connecting-state export snippet in <pre><code>; canonical HMAC-SHA256 token-binding example lives on MDN. No Chrome Platform Showcase demo exists yet (HEAD returned 404 on 2026-11-24).

Transcribed from BCD api/WebTransport.json (checked 2026-11-24) with explicit disclosure that outputLength_parameter still reads Chrome false and Safari false while Chrome 159 ships the standardized 3-argument API.

Zero unlinked citation labels; all MDN, W3C spec, IETF draft, Chromium source, WPT, BCD, webstatus.dev, ChromeStatus, Bugzilla, WebKit PR, GitHub issue, security questionnaire, and blink-dev intent links use direct <a href> with target='_blank' rel='noopener'.
